nodes.description: Adrenal insufficiency, usually presenting in the first month of life as an adrenal crisis and only rarely later in childhood with failure to thrive and recurrent vomiting. This is the life-threatening component of the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Adrenal insufficiency often presenting in the first month of life as an adrenal crisis or (rarely) later in childhood with failure to thrive and recurrent vomiting

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel heterozygous mutation, c.815T>G (p.Ile272Ser), in the CDKN1C gene in three siblings manifesting clinical symptoms associated with IMAGe syndrome and their mother (unaffected carrier).

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant in the PCNA-binding domain of the maternally expressed CDKN1C allele. All IMAGe-associated variants cluster in this domain and abolish PCNA binding, which is what distinguishes them from the Beckwith-Wiedemann variants elsewhere in the same gene.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the PCNA-binding domain of CDKN1C cause IMAGe syndrome.
evidence.snippet: All IMAGe-associated mutations clustered in the PCNA-binding domain of CDKN1C and resulted in loss of PCNA binding, distinguishing them from the mutations of CDKN1C that cause Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, an overgrowth syndrome.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous missense variants restricted to the PCNA-binding domain of the maternally expressed CDKN1C allele.

nodes.description: The core treatment, managed as for adrenal insufficiency of any cause: replacement doses of glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid plus oral sodium chloride. GeneReviews flags the specific tension to manage - steroid doses should be optimized to allow linear growth without risking an adrenal crisis, which in an undergrowth disorder is a real trade-off rather than a formality.

evidence.snippet: Chronic treatment includes replacement doses of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids and oral sodium chloride supplements.
Steroid doses should be optimized to allow for linear growth without risking an adrenal crisis.

nodes.description: Wild-type p57KIP2 is short-lived and turned over by the proteasome. IMAGe-associated mutant proteins remain stable in the presence of cycloheximide, so the variant acts by escaping degradation. This is the step that resolves an apparent paradox: loss of PCNA binding alone does not explain undergrowth, but accumulation of a cell-cycle inhibitor does.

evidence.reference_title: Increased protein stability of CDKN1C causes a gain-of-function phenotype in patients with IMAGe syndrome.
evidence.snippet: the IMAGe-associated mutant CDKN1C proteins were fairly stable even in the presence of cycloheximide, whereas the wild-type protein was almost completely degraded via the proteasome pathway

nodes.description: CDKN1C inhibits cell-cycle progression, so a stabilized, accumulating protein suppresses proliferation. Targeted expression of IMAGe-associated CDKN1C in Drosophila caused severe eye growth defects relative to wild-type CDKN1C - the in vivo demonstration that the variant is hypermorphic rather than merely non-functional.
